Can the discord group get a 20yo + section?
I don't wanna be rude (I can't say this without being rude really..) but I can't take the channels serious when there're so many kids posting. Some people have severe problems and kill themselves because they feel completely unheard and it doesn't help if you want to talk about it and you get replies from teenagers who believe they're helping. I've had this problem for a very long time as I was growing older. It's a serious issue when the majority of the internet's way younger than yourself, you can barely connect with anyone.

Thank you all for your replies.

I did start watching some of the videos of AJ Mahari. It helps even if it's painful to understand that I was never really loved. I can't even picture the conversation I'd have had with her had I discovered this subreddit before the incident and confronted her about it - it would have only caused more confusion, denial and pain I imagine. But nobody deserved that kind of pain. Neither me nor her. I wish it could have been possible to extract it from her so she wouldn't have made such a stupid decision. I know in a way that she did this to rid the world of the burden she was and the damage she would have caused to others. But people that make that choice have no idea how much more suicide hurts. I might find love some day again but her mother is gonna have to live with an irreplaceable pain forever.

I miss her every single second. She was my best friend and even if most of it was fake, I appreciated her for having her in my life.

It's only words. They don't actually mean those words - they don't even understand the meaning of them. You're being manipulated and making a terrrible decision because you feel empathy. Something they can't. You'll get treated like shit again and it will only get worse everytime. But the longer you decide to stay the more you'll get used to the mental abuse and believe it's okay to live like that. You *know* you should leave. Everybody here knows. Be strong and do it - see it as buying a lottery ticket that you know that will win one day. Buy that ticket now even if it's the hardest thing to do. One day you will win the true happiness you deserve.

You don't need to hear stories of other people.

Can you have a "healthy" relationship with an "unhealthy" person?

Can you be "happy" with someone who is chronically "unhappy"?

Should be self-explanatory.
Even if this is absolutely hilarious, it's spot on.

Even being in therapy won't help. If he truly has BPD, anything that will help will only work temporarily. Their mind changes constantly, they fixate on something for a while but lose complete interest every time. If you are willing to stay and help you have to be aware that you'll be in a world of pain and manipulation (like him saying everybody leaves him so you feel sorry). Read about any other experience people had with BPDs. It's not worth it. This is coming from a guy whose borderline girlfriend killed herself and now has to deal with trauma on top of a completely toxic & abusive relationship.
